argument_summary: The current record does not support a clean claim that the disclosure or mitigation predicate is already satisfied, and we do not add any new evidence to say otherwise. The narrower supportable position is that aggregate readiness passed, no severity-one rehearsal incidents were observed, prior approval provides limited family context, and the governing/public guidance points to disclosure and monitoring as the correct treatment path for a known limitation. On that narrower reading, the packet is not evidence that the patent prior-art triage weakness is already governed away; it is a disclosure-conditioned certification argument whose support is weak but not equivalent to a claim that the model is unsafe overall.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost argument is offered as a substitute for policy satisfaction. The only relevant operational point is that the record reflects a bounded issue in one named slice rather than a broad readiness failure, which may justify a lower risk characterization than the current score implies even though it does not cure the documentation predicate.
claims_about_policy: Policy is the limiting issue. The admissible evidence supports that current-release documentation must reflect current evaluation results and that material segment weaknesses must be disclosed or covered by an approved mitigation before certification. The same admissible evidence also shows aggregate readiness and informal monitoring are contextual only. So the policy-consistent interpretation is not clean compliance on the present record, but a narrowed, caveated position: aggregate readiness supports launch-readiness generally, while the unresolved policy defect is the absence of admissible proof that current-release disclosure or approved mitigation was completed.
concessions: No admissible evidence shows attached current-release disclosure language for the below-threshold patent prior-art triage result.
No admissible evidence shows an approved mitigation or formal risk acceptance tied to the current retrieval configuration and current evaluation batch.
Prior approval from three months ago does not by itself authorize this release.
Public model-card and AI-risk-management guidance are contextual and do not prove case-specific compliance.
